Part of the fleet-wide docs effort tracked in **rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28** (Phase 2). This repo's doc site is served under the m7kni.io hub at `/genai-otel-bridge/`, so its own Zensical build + theme overrides determine what search engines and LLMs see for these pages.

Two things are bundled here because they touch the same files:

1. **Redesign & rebrand alignment** — adopt the new m7kni.io brand and colour scheme (light-first, the shared wordmark / palette / type tokens) so the whole fleet reads as one product family. **Tune it for documentation, not marketing:** unlike the vibrant hub *landing* page, these are end-user **product documentation** sites — prioritise a clean, professional, highly readable, documentation-friendly presentation (sensible density, strong nav/TOC/search, scannable reference content) while staying on-brand in palette, type, and logo. Brand-consistent, docs-first. The exact spec follows from the hub redesign — treat the visual details as **pending finalization in rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28** and don't front-run them.
2. **SEO / LLM discoverability** — the metadata improvements below, fully specified now and able to proceed independently of the visual spec.

## Why (SEO/LLM part)

Like the hub, this site's `docs/overrides/main.html` is an empty passthrough, so OpenGraph/Twitter/JSON-LD/robots meta are either absent or (if copied from the hub) injected client-side and invisible to non-JS crawlers and LLMs (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot, social unfurlers). Render them server-side.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Redesign & rebrand alignment** — apply the finalized hub brand/scheme in a professional, documentation-friendly way (spec via rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28). Brand-consistent palette/type/logo; docs-first layout, density, and navigation.
- [ ] **Server-render head tags** — `main.html` `extrahead` override emitting canonical, `theme-color`, OpenGraph, Twitter (`summary_large_image`), and `robots` meta server-side, reading `config.extra.*` + `page.meta.*`. Mirror the hub's implementation once #29 lands (reuse the same override pattern). ⚠️ MiniJinja — no Python string methods.
- [ ] **JSON-LD** — per-page `Article` (not `TechArticle`) + a repo-level `SoftwareSourceCode`/`SoftwareApplication` node (name, description, `programmingLanguage`, `codeRepository` → this GitHub repo). `Organization` site-wide.
- [ ] **Remove any client-side `seo.js`** if this repo carries a copy; server-side supersedes it.
- [ ] **GEO content-shape pass** on the docs prose (biggest evidence-backed LLM-citation win): definition-first sentences (lead a config option with what it does), self-contained/chunkable `##`/`###` sections (restate the subject, don't rely on "it"/"this"), config/flag/env reference as **tables** not prose, language-tagged code fences (```yaml/```bash), strict one-H1-per-page hierarchy.
- [ ] **robots.txt** — ensure this repo's `docs/robots.txt` allows the current AI UAs (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent`, plus user-action bots). (Note: the hub regenerates per-site `robots.txt` at merge time — keep the source consistent with the hub's policy.)
- [ ] **Align zensical version** — match the fleet's pinned zensical version and Renovate handling as decided in Phase 1 (rknightion/m7kni-net-site#29). Depending on that decision this repo may drop zensical from its own CI entirely (if the hub build is the only consumer) or keep it pinned + Renovate-grouped for local/preview builds — follow the fleet approach from #29, don't invent a per-repo variant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Site is on-brand with the new m7kni.io scheme while reading as a clean, professional product-documentation site.
- [ ] `curl` of a deployed page under m7kni.io/genai-otel-bridge/ (no JS) shows server-rendered OG/Twitter/canonical/JSON-LD/robots meta.
- [ ] Docs pages follow the GEO content-shape checklist above.
- [ ] zensical version handling matches the fleet decision in #29.
- [ ] Site build green; renders correctly under the hub.

## Notes

- llms.txt / llms-full.txt / sitemaps for this site are generated centrally by the hub's scripts over this repo's Markdown — **not** per-repo work here.
- Do the SEO/LLM + version tasks whenever useful; gate only the visual-redesign task on the hub spec.

body:
## Problem

otlp.New builds a plain `&http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}` with no CheckRedirect, so Go's default redirect policy applies: up to 10 redirects are followed, and for 301/302/303 net/http rewrites the method to GET and drops the request body (only 307/308 preserve the POST). post() then classifies only the FINAL response: `err == nil && status >= 200 && status < 300 → return nil`. So if the configured emit endpoint (or anything in front of it — ingress, LB, auth portal, transparent proxy) answers the POST with a 302 and the redirect target answers the follow-up body-less GET with any 2xx, Emit returns nil, the runner counts EmittedSamples, and ProcessBatch advances the epoch-fenced watermark — even though zero payload bytes ever reached the gateway. The hardened httpx client used for vendor pulls deliberately blocks cross-host redirects, but the emit leg (the leg that actually carries the data) has no redirect protection at all. Empirically CONFIRMED in a throwaway worktree test: server 302s /v1/metrics → /final; observed methods=[POST GET], bodyLens=[135 0], Emit err=<nil>.

## Evidence

- `internal/emit/otlp/otlp.go:66`
- `internal/emit/otlp/otlp.go:161-167`
- `internal/emit/otlp/otlp.go:222-238`
- `internal/httpx/ (contrast: vendor-pull client blocks cross-host redirects per root CLAUDE.md 'httpx — hardened outbound client … cross-host redirect block')`

**Evidence**

```
otlp.go:66 `hc: &http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}` (no CheckRedirect); otlp.go:163 `case err == nil && status >= 200 && status < 300: … return nil`. Audit test output (worktree, since removed): `methods=[POST GET] bodyLens=[135 0] err=<nil>` — Emit reported success for a 302-then-200 chain in which the follow-up request was a GET with an empty body.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Operator points emit.telemetry.otlp.endpoint at an in-cluster collector or gateway fronted by an ingress/LB that issues a 301 http→https or trailing-slash redirect (Traefik's http→https default is 301; many LBs 302 to a portal that answers 200 to GET). Every tick: POST is converted to a body-less GET, the 200 response marks the batch emitted, the watermark advances past the window — the entire loop's data is silently and permanently lost (the forward-only watermark never re-pulls it), with emitted_samples counters even reporting success. This is the exact 'silent gap/drop' the operational-honesty rule forbids. (If the GET instead gets a 405/404 the loop at least halts loudly — the 2xx-responding case is the silent one.)

## Suggested direction

Set `CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse }` on the emit client so a 3xx surfaces as its own status code (falls into the default branch → RetryableError, no advance, alertable via emit_errors_total), or explicitly return an error on any redirect. Add a regression test mirroring the audit test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A 301/302/303/307/308 response from the emit endpoint never results in Emit returning nil
- [ ] The 3xx outcome is loud (RetryableError or RejectError with a counter/alert path) and never advances the watermark
- [ ] Regression test: httptest server that 302s /v1/metrics to a 200-answering path asserts Emit returns a non-nil error and the origin never received a body-less GET counted as success

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — Citation otlp.go:161-167 is marginally off — the 2xx success branch is lines 162-167 (line 161 is the switch keyword). Not a documented deferral: followup.md line 32 mentions the plain http.Client only in the context of a missing loop.emit observability span, not the redirect hazard, so this is a genuine unacknowledged bug.

body:
## Problem

lead()'s renew-deadline enforcement is purely synchronous: `renewDeadline` is only compared (dynamodb.go:183) AFTER `c.renew()` returns, inside the `<-ticker.C` case, and there is no watchdog that cancels leaderCtx independently. `renew()` issues UpdateItem with leaderCtx, which has no deadline and is only ever cancelled by this same loop. buildHA constructs the DynamoDB client with SDK defaults (main.go:294-309) — aws-sdk-go-v2's default BuildableClient has clientTimeout=0 and no ResponseHeaderTimeout (aws/transport/http/client.go), so an established-but-silent connection hangs indefinitely, and even the common blackholed-endpoint case costs 30s dial timeout x 3 standard-retryer attempts (~90s) per renew. Contrast the K8s path: client-go wraps every renew in context.WithTimeout(ctx, RenewDeadline) (leaderelection.go:317), so a hung apiserver call steps the leader down at RenewDeadline. The design's in-flight single-emit fence IS leaderCtx cancellation (lease.go:99-100, schedule CLAUDE.md 'commit() re-checks ctx.Err() before Save'); a renew stall means that fence never fires.

## Evidence

- `internal/coordinate/dynamodb/dynamodb.go:132-152`
- `internal/coordinate/dynamodb/dynamodb.go:161-189`
- `cmd/genai-otel-bridge/main.go:294-309`
- `internal/coordinate/lease/lease.go:99-100 (leaderCtx cancellation is 'the real in-flight fence')`

**Evidence**

```
dynamodb.go:172-189: `case <-ticker.C: ok, err := c.renew(leaderCtx, fence)` ... `default: if c.now().Sub(lastRenew) >= c.renewDeadline { ... cancel() }` — the deadline check is unreachable while renew blocks. renew(): `_, err := c.db.UpdateItem(ctx, ...)` with no WithTimeout. SDK default: `clientTimeout time.Duration` zero-valued, transport sets no ResponseHeaderTimeout (aws/transport/http/client.go:23-35,175-192). client-go comparator: `timeoutCtx, timeoutCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, le.config.RenewDeadline)` (leaderelection.go:317).
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Leader A's path to DynamoDB degrades (VPC-endpoint blackhole, NACL change, silent peer) while its vendor/OTLP egress (NAT/internet) stays up. A's renew hangs; its lock item expires at lastRenew+15s and standby B acquires with fence+1 and starts emitting. A's scheduler keeps collecting and emitting the same windows because leaderCtx is never cancelled — for ~75s in the 30s-dial x 3-attempts case, and FOREVER in the hung-connection case (only SIGTERM unblocks). DESIGN.md F11 assumes split-brain is 'brief'; here it is unbounded: doubled vendor-API and export-job load, duplicate Loki log emission, and growing probability of value-divergent edge buckets -> Mimir duplicate-timestamp 400 churn. A's checkpoint saves are epoch-fenced once B saves (no double-advance), but single-active-replica is violated for the whole stall.

## Suggested direction

Run each renew under context.WithTimeout(leaderCtx, <=retry or remaining renewDeadline), and/or enforce renewDeadline with a timer that cancels leaderCtx regardless of an in-flight call (client-go parity). Optionally set an overall client timeout on the DynamoDB client in buildHA.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A renew UpdateItem that blocks longer than renew_deadline results in leaderCtx cancellation no later than ~renew_deadline after the last successful renew (unit test with a fake UpdateAPI that blocks on a channel)
- [ ] A test proves onElected's ctx is cancelled while a renew call is still in flight
- [ ] No change to the acquire/renew condition expressions or the fence bump semantics

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — The 'evidence' block labels the renewDeadline check as a select `default:` case; it is actually the `default:` branch of the INNER switch over the renew result (the cited line range 172-189 is otherwise accurate). The 'FOREVER (only SIGTERM unblocks)' wording is the application-level hang sub-case (an LB/proxy holding the TCP connection open with no HTTP response); a pure packet blackhole on an already-established connection would eventually be terminated by the OS TCP retransmission timeout (~13-30 min, tcp_retries2-dependent) — still vastly exceeding the 10s renewDeadline, so 'unbounded relative to design intent' is accurate even if literal-forever is only the proxy-hold case. Neither correction affects the verdict or severity.

body:
## Problem

Container-definition `secrets` (valueFrom: Secrets Manager ARN) are fetched by the ECS agent using the task EXECUTION role, not the task role. The vendored terraform-aws-modules/ecs service submodule (v7.5.0) only adds a `GetSecrets` statement to the exec-role policy when `task_exec_secret_arns` is passed (dynamic block gated on `length(var.task_exec_secret_arns) > 0`); the repo's module call never sets it, so the module-created exec role carries only Logs+ECR. Meanwhile main.tf grants `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` to the TASK role (locals.task_iam_statements `SecretsRead`), which the app never uses — secrets arrive as injected env vars, and the binary makes no Secrets Manager calls.

## Evidence

- `deploy/ecs/terraform/main.tf:91-98`
- `deploy/ecs/terraform/main.tf:318-320`
- `deploy/ecs/terraform/main.tf:70`
- `deploy/ecs/terraform/.terraform/modules/service/modules/service/main.tf:1161-1168`
- `deploy/ecs/terraform/README.md:48-53`

**Evidence**

```
main.tf:91-98: `sid = "SecretsRead" ... actions = ["secretsmanager:GetSecretValue"]` inside `task_iam_statements` (injected via tasks_iam_role_statements = TASK role). Vendored module main.tf:1161-1168: `dynamic "statement" { for_each = length(var.task_exec_secret_arns) > 0 ? [1] : [] ... sid = "GetSecrets" }` — and `task_exec_secret_arns` defaults to [] and is never passed by deploy/ecs/terraform/main.tf.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Following the README quick-start (secret_arns = {GC_OTLP_ENDPOINT, GC_INSTANCE_ID, GC_OTLP_TOKEN, PORTKEY_API_KEY}), every task launch fails with `ResourceInitializationError: unable to pull secrets or registry auth ... AccessDeniedException` — the ECS service never reaches RUNNING, so the advertised production-grade ECS deployment is dead on arrival for any real configuration (all real configs need at least the GC + vendor credentials).

## Suggested direction

Pass `task_exec_secret_arns = values(var.secret_arns)` to module.service (plus a kms:Decrypt exec-role statement via task_exec_iam_statements when the secrets are CMK-encrypted), and drop the now-unnecessary SecretsRead statement from the task role (least-privilege: the app itself never calls Secrets Manager).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] module.service receives task_exec_secret_arns covering every ARN in var.secret_arns
- [ ] The task role policy no longer carries secretsmanager:GetSecretValue (or a comment justifies keeping it)
- [ ] tofu validate + tflint + checkov still pass (make tf-validate)
- [ ] README/IAM comments updated to state which role fetches container-def secrets

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — Minor citation precision: the SecretsRead statement spans main.tf:91-98 within the locals block that starts at line 81, and it is injected into the task role at line 284 (the finding's citation of :91-98 is correct; the injection site 284 is worth noting). The KMS angle in the suggested fix only matters for customer-managed-key-encrypted secrets — the AWS-managed aws/secretsmanager default key does not require an explicit exec-role kms:Decrypt (granted via the key policy), so the core GetSecretValue gap is the blocking issue regardless of kms_key_arn.

body:
## Problem

values.yaml pins `image: ghcr.io/rknightion/genai-otel-bridge:latest@sha256:6b8946...` (Renovate docker:pinDigests). The `:latest` tag only moves on releases (publish.sh: main builds tag `main <sha>`, releases tag `vX.Y.Z latest`), and Renovate can only bump the digest AFTER an image is pushed — so at the moment the release PR merges, the committed digest is necessarily the PREVIOUS release's image. The chart is then packaged from that tagged commit (publish.sh:101 / shared container-publish.yml:395 set only --version/--app-version; neither rewrites the image line, verified in the pinned reusable workflow — its IMAGE_DIGEST env is declared but unused). release-please's extra-files bump only Chart.yaml. Combined with config.go:373 `dec.KnownFields(true)` (unknown YAML key ⇒ load error) and the chart's generated `config:` block surfacing every schema knob at its default, a release that ADDS any config key ships a chart whose default configmap contains a key the pinned (previous) binary rejects.

## Evidence

- `deploy/helm/values.yaml:12`
- `scripts/publish.sh:99-102`
- `release-please-config.json:11-13`
- `internal/config/config.go:373`
- `CLAUDE.md:107-109`
- `deploy/helm/templates/deployment.yaml:100`
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml:32-42`
- `CLAUDE.md:116-117`
- `commit 09d516d (chore(deps): pin dependencies #11)`

**Evidence**

```
values.yaml:12 `image: ghcr.io/rknightion/genai-otel-bridge:latest@sha256:6b8946d9...`; publish.sh:59 `image_tags="${RELEASE_TAG} latest"` vs :67 `image_tags="main ${short}"`; shared workflow chart step runs only `helm package "${CHART_PATH}" --version ... --app-version ...`; config.go:373 `dec.KnownFields(true) // unknown YAML key ⇒ error`.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Release vN adds a governance knob (as v3.x releases did). `helm install` of chart vN with default values renders the new key into genai-otel-bridge-config, but the pinned digest is the vN-1 image; the binary fatals `load config: unknown YAML key` and the Deployment CrashLoopBackOffs — a fresh default install of the current chart release is broken until the operator manually overrides `image`. ## Suggested direction

- [ ] A chart published for tag vX.Y.Z default-installs the vX.Y.Z image (verifiable from the packaged tgz values)

body:
## Problem

The uninstall cleanup ALWAYS deletes the Lease ('pure ephemeral coordination state', cleanup.go:23-25) even when retainCheckpoint keeps the ConfigMap. But the checkpoint durably stores the leader epoch (Watermark.Epoch = Lease.Spec.LeaseTransitions, persisted by the configmap store), and checkpoint.CheckMonotonic rejects any Save whose incoming.Epoch < stored.Epoch (checkpoint.go:34-35). A reinstall creates a FRESH lease whose LeaseTransitions is nil -> epoch() returns 0 (lease.go:110-113). If the previous install ever had >=1 leadership transition (any pod restart, rollout, or failover increments LeaseTransitions), the retained checkpoint's stored epoch N>=1 > new epoch 0, so EVERY Save returns ErrStaleWrite; runner.commit's fenced branch (runner.go:311-318) resyncs the frontier to durable and never advances. The dynamodb coordinator explicitly designed around this exact hazard class (dynamodb.go:93-96: 'auto-deletion of the lock would reset fence ... permanently fencing all writes'), but the K8s cleanup path recreates it.

## Evidence

- `internal/cleanup/cleanup.go:23-25`
- `cmd/genai-otel-bridge/main.go:58-59`
- `deploy/helm/values.yaml:449-453`
- `internal/coordinate/lease/lease.go:103-113`
- `internal/checkpoint/checkpoint.go:33-35`
- `internal/schedule/runner.go:305-318`
- `internal/coordinate/dynamodb/dynamodb.go:93-96`

**Evidence**

```
cleanup.go: 'The lease is ALWAYS removed: it is pure ephemeral coordination state.' vs checkpoint.go CheckMonotonic: 'return fmt.Errorf("%w: epoch %d < stored %d", ErrStaleWrite, incoming.Epoch, stored.Epoch)' and lease.go epoch(): 'if l.Spec.LeaseTransitions == nil { return 0 }'
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Operator runs `helm uninstall` with cleanup.retainCheckpoint=true after the install has had at least one leadership transition (near-certain after any rollout), then reinstalls expecting the advertised watermark resume (values.yaml:449-451). The new leader collects from the retained watermark, emits, and the commit is epoch-fenced every tick: window_lag grows unboundedly, checkpoint_fenced fires each tick, and the logs loops re-collect and re-emit the SAME window every tick — Loki has no dedupe, so duplicate log records accumulate downstream — until LeaseTransitions accrues past the stored epoch N (N further restarts) or an operator hand-edits the checkpoint.

## Suggested direction

Either retain the Lease too when retainCheckpoint is set, strip/zero the Epoch fields when retaining (a fresh install legitimately starts a new epoch domain), or floor the elected epoch at the durable checkpoint's max epoch on first election. Whatever the fix, add a reinstall-with-retained-checkpoint test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test proving: install -> save watermark at epoch>=1 -> cleanup with retain -> reinstall (fresh lease, epoch 0) -> watermark advances on the first commit
- [ ] No checkpoint_fenced storm after a retain-reinstall cycle
- [ ] values.yaml / cleanup docs updated to describe the actual resume semantics

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — Minor: the title's 'permanently fences' is slightly overstated — the finding body is correct that it self-heals once post-reinstall LeaseTransitions accrues to ≥ N (or via a manual ConfigMap edit). In a stable install those transitions are days/weeks apart, so the stall + duplicate-emit window is long-lived but not literally permanent. Also note the failure is loud/alertable (checkpoint_fenced fires, window_lag grows) rather than silent, so an operator would observe it — a genuine mitigating factor. Scope is precisely the K8s lease-coordinator path with cleanup.retainCheckpoint=true; the DynamoDB path is safe by design and unaffected.

body:
## Problem

The signed-URL object download does `resp, err := l.dlClient.Do(req); if err != nil { return nil, 0, false, err }` and returns the RAW Go transport error. On a non-2xx status the code uses httpx.ErrSnippet (bounded body, no URL), but on any transport-level error (timeout, connection reset, EOF, TLS error) the returned error is a *url.Error whose string embeds the FULL request URL including its query string. A Portkey/S3 signed download URL carries its authorization in the query (e.g. X-Amz-Signature / X-Goog-Signature / SAS token) — that query string IS a time-limited bearer credential granting read access to the raw export object (which contains un-stripped metadata/PII, since the content strip is client-side after download). This error propagates up through stepDownloading -> Collect -> scheduler.go:195 `slog.Warn("collect failed", ..., "err", err)`, writing the full presigned URL to stdout, which k8s-monitoring/Alloy scrapes into Loki — the observability backend. Verified empirically: `http.Client.Get` on an unreachable presigned-style URL yields `Get "http://host/obj?X-Amz-Signature=SUPERSECRETSIG&...": dial tcp ...: connection refused` — the signature is in the log line.

## Evidence

- `internal/source/portkey/logs_download.go:81-84`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_client.go:94-103`
- `internal/schedule/scheduler.go:195`
- `internal/httpx/httpx.go:136-142`

**Evidence**

```
logs_download.go:81  resp, err := l.dlClient.Do(req)
logs_download.go:83      return nil, 0, false, err  // raw *url.Error embeds ?X-Amz-Signature=...
scheduler.go:195  slog.Warn("collect failed", "loop", name, "err", err)
```

## Failure scenario / impact

A large export object download times out or the S3 connection is reset mid-transfer (routine for multi-hundred-MiB objects) -> the *url.Error containing the full presigned download URL (with X-Amz-Signature) is logged to stdout -> lands in Loki, where anyone with Loki read access can copy the URL and download the raw, un-stripped export (metadata/PII) for the URL's ~6h validity window. Violates both the secrets-never-logged and content-minimisation invariants.

## Suggested direction

Wrap the download transport error so the signed URL is never rendered: return a sanitized error (e.g. status/host only, or url.Redacted()-style with the query stripped) instead of the raw *url.Error. Same treatment for getDownloadURL if it ever surfaces a URL. Consider a shared httpx helper that strips the query from any *url.Error, and a regression test asserting the signature never appears in the returned error string.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A transport error during signed-URL download produces an error string that contains neither the query string nor any X-Amz-Signature/X-Goog-Signature/SAS token
- [ ] A test injects a failing signed-URL fetch (with a signature-bearing query) and asserts the resulting Collect error / logged err contains no signature
- [ ] ErrSnippet-based non-2xx path is unchanged (already safe)

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED

## Problem

bufio.Scanner with Buffer(..., maxLogLineBytes=1MiB) aborts the whole scan with ErrTooLong when any line exceeds the cap — it cannot skip past the line. downloadChunk returns that as an error (logs_download.go:134-135); stepDownloading returns the error verbatim and discards even the records read before the long line (logs_export.go:316-319), so PageOffsetDone never advances. The S3 object is stable, so every retry re-reads the same bytes and errors identically. Unlike a stuck job (job_poll_timeout -> cancel+restart) there is NO abandon path from phaseDownloading, and maxLogLineBytes is an untunable const (no test covers this path). The package CLAUDE.md and the maxLogLineBytes comment claim such a line is 'treated as malformed... and skipped loudly' — the code does not skip it.

## Evidence

- `internal/source/portkey/logs_download.go:29`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_download.go:100`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_download.go:134-135`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_export.go:316-319`
- `internal/source/portkey/CLAUDE.md:171`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_download.go:27-29`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_download.go:99-100`

**Evidence**

```
logs_download.go:100 `sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), maxLogLineBytes)`; :134 `if serr := sc.Err(); serr != nil { return recs, linesRead, false, fmt.Errorf(...) }`; logs_export.go:316-319 `recs, lines, eof, err := l.downloadChunk(...); if err != nil { return model.Batch{}, err }` (partial recs and line progress discarded). Worktree test output: 'attempt 1: err=portkey logs_export: stream signed-url body: bufio.Scanner: token too long, linesRead=1' and 'retry errs identically — line offset can never pass the over-long line'.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

One export record whose Portkey-injected metadata/portkeyHeaders blob (injected regardless of requested_data, PoC §3) pushes its JSONL line past 1MiB -> every Collect on that window errors 'bufio.Scanner: token too long', the cursor stays in phaseDownloading forever, Watermark.Time never advances, and the logs plane stops delivering permanently — recoverable only by manual checkpoint surgery (window_lag grows and errors log, so it is loud, but there is no self-healing or config escape). Empirically confirmed in a worktree test: retry consumes the identical line count and errors identically.

## Suggested direction

Replace the Scanner with a line reader that can detect and SKIP an over-long line while still advancing the line offset (counting it via OnGraphSkipped, e.g. graph="line_oversize"), matching the documented skip-loudly semantics; alternatively make maxLogLineBytes a setting and add a downloading-phase abandon deadline that resets the window like export_stuck.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test feeds downloadChunk an object containing a line > maxLogLineBytes surrounded by good lines and asserts the good lines are emitted, the offset advances past the bad line, and a self-metric/hook fires
- [ ] stepDownloading eventually completes a window containing an over-long line (or abandons it via a bounded, counted path) — never retries the same offset forever
- [ ] CLAUDE.md / code comments match the actual behaviour
- [ ] A >maxLogLineBytes line in a page is skipped with a loud counter and the page/window still completes
- [ ] A regression test covers the oversize-line path
- [ ] The maxLogLineBytes comment matches the real behaviour

**Also covers (same root cause):**
- A single JSONL export line over 1 MiB permanently stalls the portkey logs_export loop (retry-forever on identical bytes), while the code comment claims the line is skipped

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — The doc skip-loud claim is at portkey/CLAUDE.md line 170, not 171. Otherwise citations accurate. The download-error wedge is loud only via window_lag + error log — it does NOT fire the OnGraphSkipped/graph_unavailable self-metric (jobFailed is only called in stepPolling for export_stuck/export_failed); the finding states this correctly.

## Problem

The old pipeline (scripts/publish.sh:60-63) tagged release images `image_tags="${RELEASE_TAG} latest"` i.e. `:v1.2.3`, and set appVersion `v1.2.3`. The shared reusable (rknightion/.github container-publish.yml, merge job) tags via docker/metadata-action `type=semver,pattern={{version}},value=<release-tag>` — metadata-action's {{version}} strips the leading `v`, so releases now publish `:1.2.3` + `:1.2` + `:1` + `:latest`, and the helm job sets appVersion `${RELEASE_TAG#v}` (no v). No release has been cut since the migration (last release 3.0.1 predates 5e59ce5), so the registry currently holds only v-prefixed release tags; the scheme flips on the next release. docs/installation.md:109 (`--set image=ghcr.io/rknightion/genai-otel-bridge:v1.0.0`) and values.yaml:11's comment still teach the v-prefixed form.

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/publish.yml:39-42`
- `scripts/publish.sh:60-63`
- `docs/installation.md:109`
- `deploy/helm/values.yaml:11`
- `commit 5e59ce5 (ci: publish image + Helm chart via shared container-publish reusable)`

**Evidence**

```
Old: scripts/publish.sh `image_tags="${RELEASE_TAG} latest"` (v-prefixed). New: reusable meta step `type=semver,pattern={{version}},value=${{ inputs.release-tag }}` (metadata-action strips the v) + helm job `version="${RELEASE_TAG#v}"; appversion="${RELEASE_TAG#v}"`. docs/installation.md:109 still: `--set image=ghcr.io/rknightion/genai-otel-bridge:v1.0.0`.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

After v3.1.0 is released, a user follows docs/installation.md and sets `image: ghcr.io/rknightion/genai-otel-bridge:v3.1.0` — that tag does not exist under the new pipeline, so the pod goes ImagePullBackOff. Conversely, tooling that pulls `:3.0.1` for the current release also 404s. Mixed v/no-v tag history makes registry automation (digest pinning, semver-range trackers) inconsistent across the boundary.

## Suggested direction

Decide one scheme. If keeping the reusable's no-v scheme, update docs/installation.md, values.yaml's comment, and CLAUDE.md's Release wording; optionally add a one-off `type=raw,value=${{ inputs.release-tag }}` style alias for continuity with existing v-prefixed tags.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The documented `--set image=` examples name a tag format the release pipeline actually publishes
- [ ] The next release's published image tags are verified against the docs (e.g. crane/gh package listing)
- [ ] CLAUDE.md Release section states the actual tag scheme

body:
## Problem

config.Duration decodes negative values ('-10m') fine via time.ParseDuration, and Validate has no non-negativity checks on these three loop fields (it does check negativity on all four governance ints, so the omission is an inconsistency, not a policy). Empirically verified in a worktree: configs with bucket_settle=-10m and max_backfill=-1h both return nil from Validate. Downstream, portkey's Collect computes until=now-settle → now+10m, so buckets younger than settle (including the current in-progress minute) are emitted immediately; when the vendor later revises those buckets, the settle-exceedance path counts but never re-emits (DESIGN §3.3/F6) — the emitted value is permanently wrong. Negative max_backfill makes the scheduler's backfill floor sit in the future, firing backfill_unstorable spuriously every tick and clamping collect starts nonsensically.

## Evidence

- `internal/config/config.go:600-628 (loop checks: cadence floor catches <=0 cadence and window checks catch negative window, but no >=0 check on BucketSettle/MaxBackfill/BootstrapLookback)`
- `internal/config/config.go:621-624 (negative settle LOWERS the window lower bound, so the M3 check passes more easily)`
- `internal/config/config.go:625 (`MaxBackfill > 0 &&` guard means a negative max_backfill skips the bootstrap sanity check entirely)`
- `internal/source/portkey/portkey.go:255 (`until := now.Add(-l.settle)` — negative settle puts the collect upper bound in the FUTURE)`
- `internal/schedule/scheduler.go:174-176 (negative MaxBackfill puts floor=now+|d| in the future → wm.Time.Before(floor) every tick → spurious backfill_unstorable counts)`

**Evidence**

```
Worktree tests: `negative bucket_settle Validate err: <nil>` and `negative max_backfill Validate err: <nil>`; portkey.go:255 `until := now.Add(-l.settle)`
```

## Failure scenario / impact

A templating mistake or sign error produces `bucket_settle: -10m`. Startup and -validate-config both succeed. Every poll emits still-changing buckets; Portkey's late arrivals (measured ~3m settling) revise them afterwards, but emit-once discards the revisions — Mimir permanently holds undercounted request/cost/token series with no gap signal, only the bucket_revised_after_settle counter rising. This is a direct crack in the emit-once-after-settle leg of the correctness contract that fail-fast validation is supposed to guard.

## Suggested direction

Reject negative Cadence/Window/BucketSettle/BootstrapLookback/MaxBackfill in Validate for enabled loops (and negative ha.dynamodb lease durations while there — lease_duration=-5s/renew=-10s currently passes the `lease > renew` check). One loop over the fields with a `< 0` check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Validate rejects a negative value in any per-loop Duration field with a message naming the field
- [ ] Negative ha.dynamodb.lease_duration/renew_deadline are rejected
- [ ] Regression tests for negative bucket_settle and max_backfill

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED

Empirically verified: `rate: Wait(n=1) exceeds limiter's burst 0` for both (rps=0,burst=0) and (rps=1,burst=0); and a config with a zeroed RateLimitConfig passes cfg.Validate (worktree test).

- `internal/config/config.go:297-301 (RateLimitConfig has helm defaults only; no Load default, no Validate check)`
- `internal/config/config.go:577-628 (per-source Validate loop — no rps/burst check)`
- `internal/source/portkey/portkey.go:107 (rate.NewLimiter(rate.Limit(cfg.RateLimit.RPS), cfg.RateLimit.Burst) — raw passthrough)`
- `internal/source/langsmith/langsmith.go:153 (same passthrough)`
- `internal/httpx/httpx.go:111-113 (Limiter.Wait called before every request)`

```
go run demo: `limit=0 burst=0: err=rate: Wait(n=1) exceeds limiter's burst 0` and `limit=1 burst=0: err=rate: Wait(n=1) exceeds limiter's burst 0`; worktree test: zeroed RateLimitConfig passes cfg.Validate(known)
```

An operator hand-writes a config (ECS env-injected, or any non-Helm deployment) and omits the `rate_limit:` block, or sets rps without burst. Startup succeeds and -validate-config reports OK, but every Collect fails before any request reaches the vendor — the loop never collects a single sample, the watermark never advances, and the on-call is left debugging a cryptic limiter error that looks nothing like a config mistake. ## Problem

Loop names are free-form map keys in config; each vendor constructor reads only the fixed names it knows and never diffs the config map against them, and neither Validate nor app.Build reconciles configured loop names against constructed loops. Empirically verified in a throwaway worktree: a source with an enabled `analytics` loop plus an enabled `log_export` (typo of logs_export) loop passes cfg.Validate (nil) and reg.Build returns only [analytics] — the typo'd stanza vanishes with zero log output. The codebase's own conventions treat this as forbidden: unknown settings keys WARN, unknown graph names fail fast (CP-H4), unknown YAML fields error (KnownFields).

## Evidence

- `internal/config/config.go:600-628 (Validate checks cadence/window math for every map entry regardless of name — a typo'd loop looks validated)`
- `internal/source/portkey/portkey.go:49-51 (only "analytics"/"groups"/"logs_export" keys are read)`
- `internal/source/langsmith/langsmith.go:76-78 (only "sessions"/"runs"/"usage")`
- `internal/app/app.go:125-148 (Build wires only loops the source returned; no reconciliation against cfg loop names)`
- `internal/source/langsmith/settings.go:119-123 (contrast: unknown settings KEYS at least WARN, with an explicit operationally-honest rationale)`

**Evidence**

```
Worktree test output: `loops built: [analytics] (typo'd log_export silently absent)` after cfg.Validate returned nil for the same config
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Operator enables Portkey metrics and adds the logs plane but types `log_export:` (or `logs-export`, or `session:`). Deploy succeeds, validation passes (the stanza's cadence/window are even checked, reinforcing false confidence), metrics flow — and the entire logs plane silently never collects. No error, no warning, no metric distinguishes 'loop disabled by typo' from 'loop not configured'. Only guarded when the typo'd loop is the sole enabled loop (then Build errors 'no enabled loops').

Have each source declare its known loop names (or have New return an error/warn on unrecognised enabled loop names), and/or make app.Build fail fast when an enabled configured loop name was not constructed by its source. A registry-level `KnownLoops(type)` keeps the check decoupled.

## Problem

The documented fallback to emit.telemetry applies only when the whole `emit.self` block is nil (main.go:173). If an operator sets `emit.self:` with any sub-key (e.g. only `metric_interval: 120s`) but no `otlp.endpoint`, validateEmitEndpoint short-circuits on the empty endpoint (config.go:641 `ep == ""` → nil), Validate passes, selfobs.NewProvider constructs without error, and the PeriodicReader exports to the malformed URL `http:///v1/metrics`. Empirically verified in a throwaway worktree: NewProvider err=nil, then ForceFlush fails with `Post "http:///v1/metrics": http: no Host in request URL`. Self-APM tracing uses the same selfEP and breaks identically.

## Evidence

- `internal/config/config.go:639-643 (validateEmitEndpoint returns nil when ep=="")`
- `internal/config/config.go:538-551 (Emit.Self validation checks only metric_interval and the endpoint gate)`
- `cmd/genai-otel-bridge/main.go:171-176 (selfEP = cfg.Emit.Self.OTLP whenever the self block is non-nil; fallback only when nil)`
- `internal/selfobs/provider.go:34-37 (WithEndpointURL(strings.TrimRight("", "/")+"/v1/metrics"))`
- `internal/config/config.go:187 (doc: "optional separate self-telemetry endpoint; falls back to emit.telemetry")`

**Evidence**

```
config.go:641: `if ep == "" || !insecureURL(ep) || loopbackURL(ep) { return nil }`; empirical test: `NewProvider err=<nil>` then `ForceFlush err=failed to upload metrics: Post "http:///v1/metrics": http: no Host in request URL`
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Operator adds `emit: { self: { metric_interval: 120s } }` to slow the self-metric rate, expecting the documented endpoint fallback. Startup succeeds, -validate-config says OK, product telemetry flows — but every self-obs export fails forever. All alerting signals (window_lag, samples_skipped_total, auth_errors_total, guard drops, health-adjacent metrics) silently stop reaching Grafana Cloud; the only trace is a periodic otel exporter error line in stdout. The operational-honesty layer itself is the thing that dies, so nothing alerts on it.

## Suggested direction

In Validate, when c.Emit.Self != nil require a non-empty c.Emit.Self.OTLP.Endpoint (or implement per-field fallback to telemetry in main.go and document it). A one-line errs append mirrors the existing emit.telemetry.otlp.endpoint-required check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A config with emit.self present and emit.self.otlp.endpoint empty fails Validate with a clear error (or demonstrably falls back to the telemetry endpoint end-to-end)
- [ ] Existing configs with a fully-specified emit.self and configs with no emit.self block still validate
- [ ] A regression test covers the partial emit.self block case

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED

## Problem

internal/config/config.go's LoopConfig defaults are `bucket_settle: 10m` and `max_backfill: 90m`; internal/config/CLAUDE.md explicitly documents that these were raised from the older `3m`/`55m` values because '3m was insufficient' (live-measured late-arrival lag) and 90m was sized to leave margin under Mimir's 2h out-of-order window. docs/configuration.md's own example already uses the current `10m`/`90m` values. But README.md's Quickstart config block and docs/installation.md's 'Write a config file' example both still show `bucket_settle: 3m` / `max_backfill: 55m` — the exact values the internal docs say were found insufficient/superseded.

## Evidence

- `README.md:49-50`
- `docs/installation.md:57-58`
- `docs/configuration.md:122-123`
- `internal/config/config.go:315,322`
- `internal/config/CLAUDE.md:22,24-26`

## Failure scenario / impact

A new user copy-pastes the README or installation.md Quickstart config verbatim into production. Their analytics loop settles buckets after only 3 minutes (below the live-measured late-arrival lag margin that motivated raising the default to 10m), producing more `bucket_revised_after_settle_total` events (settled values that later change and can never be corrected, since Mimir rejects a changed value at an already-emitted timestamp) than the shipped default would, and their `max_backfill: 55m` leaves far less margin under Mimir's 2-hour out-of-order acceptance window during an outage than the 90m the maintainers now recommend.

## Suggested direction

Update the Quickstart config blocks in README.md and docs/installation.md to use `bucket_settle: 10m` / `max_backfill: 90m`, matching docs/configuration.md and the actual Go defaults.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README.md's Quickstart example uses bucket_settle: 10m and max_backfill: 90m
- [ ] docs/installation.md's config example uses the same current defaults

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED

body:
## Problem

coordinate.Noop stamps epoch 1 unconditionally (coordinate.go:36). CheckMonotonic rejects any incoming.Epoch < stored.Epoch (checkpoint.go:34-35). Both the lease epoch (LeaseTransitions) and the dynamodb fence exceed 1 after the second-ever leadership transition/acquire, and the checkpoint stores that epoch durably. Nothing in config validation or the checkpoint path detects or documents the downgrade; ErrStaleWrite is exempt from the degraded/save-fail counter (runner.go:294-304), so the loop never backs off — it resyncs its frontier to the stuck durable watermark (runner.go:317) and retries at full cadence forever.

## Evidence

- `internal/coordinate/coordinate.go:32-38`
- `internal/checkpoint/checkpoint.go:34-36`
- `internal/schedule/runner.go:294-319`
- `internal/config/config.go:511`

**Evidence**

```
coordinate.go:36 `onElected(WithEpoch(ctx, 1))`; checkpoint.go:34 `if incoming.Epoch < stored.Epoch { return ErrStaleWrite }`; runner.go:305-319 fenced path resyncs frontier and returns without incrementing saveFails (no degrade, full-cadence retry).
```

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator scales an HA deployment down and sets ha.coordinator: none (a documented valid value, config.go:511) while keeping the same checkpoint store (configmap or dynamodb) whose stored epoch is >= 2. Every Save is rejected with the epoch fence: the runner re-collects the SAME window each tick, re-emits it (duplicate emission at full cadence against the vendor API and the gateway), fires checkpoint_fenced continuously, and durable progress is frozen. It never self-heals — recovery requires manually deleting the checkpoint objects, and any restart in the meantime re-pulls from the frozen watermark.

## Suggested direction

Either have Noop adopt max(1, stored epoch) semantics — e.g. Save-side: treat a Noop/none deployment as epoch >= stored — or fail-fast/warn at startup when coordinator=none finds a checkpoint with epoch above Noop's constant; at minimum document the migration trap and the manual-deletion recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test where a checkpoint saved at epoch 3 is followed by a Noop-coordinated run: watermark writes must either succeed or the process must fail loudly at startup with actionable guidance (not spin re-emitting)
- [ ] Tracked docs describe the lease/dynamodb -> none migration behavior

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — The finding is accurate. Minor citation fix: config.go:511 is the *invalid-value* error line; the "none is a documented valid value" claim is anchored at config.go:509 (`case "lease", "none", "dynamodb":`). One clarification the finding underweights: the fenced state is NOT silent — it fires `checkpoint_fenced` (runner.go:313) continuously and window_lag grows, so it is alertable per the project's "operationally honest" hard rule; the harm is a permanent, self-non-healing stall requiring manual checkpoint deletion, not silent data loss. This is a genuine unguarded gap in the same "permanently fence writes" hazard class the team explicitly defended against in ARCHITECTURE.md ledger #17 (for the dynamodb outage case) — the coordinator=none downgrade is the uncovered analogue and warrants at minimum a startup warn/fail plus a documented migration note.

comments.body:
Partially addressed in a17b740 (Wave 1a). The **mechanism** is now in place: `coordinate.Noop` stamps `max(1, Epoch)` (was a constant 1), a `NoopWithEpoch(e)` constructor exists, and `buildHA` now emits a loud startup WARN when `ha.coordinator=none` is configured over a durable (configmap/dynamodb) checkpoint. Regression tests `TestNoopEpochMaxSemantics` / `TestNoopEpochAvoidsCheckpointFence` cover the epoch semantics.

**Still open — the auto-heal wiring.** True fail-fast/auto-heal needs `buildHA` to read the *stored* epoch and pass it to `NoopWithEpoch`, but that requires enumerating checkpoint keys by `OutputFingerprint`, which is only known after the source graph is built in `internal/app`. Wiring max-stored-epoch → `NoopWithEpoch` therefore belongs in the app/schedule composition layer, not in the coordinate package. Until that lands, a downgrade to `coordinator=none` over a real epoch≥2 checkpoint still spins until the operator deletes the checkpoint — but it is now loud (the startup WARN), not silent.

Keeping this open to track the app-layer wiring pass.

body:
## Problem

config.Validate only enforces lease_duration > renew_deadline and retry_period > 0 (config.go:528-532). The renew ticker cadence IS retry_period (dynamodb.go:161), so with retry_period >= lease_duration the lock expires between renew ticks on every term. client-go rejects the analogous misconfiguration outright (renewDeadline must be > retryPeriod*1.2, leaderelection.go:80); the K8s path is safe only because its 15s/10s/2s params are hardcoded in main.go, while the dynamodb params are operator-configurable. dynamodb.go:43's comment claims 'lease > renewDeadline > 0 and retry > 0 (validated upstream)' — nothing orders retry relative to the other two.

## Evidence

- `internal/config/config.go:528-532`
- `internal/coordinate/dynamodb/dynamodb.go:161-163`
- `internal/coordinate/dynamodb/dynamodb.go:43`

**Evidence**

```
config.go:528-532 validates only `LeaseDuration <= RenewDeadline` and `RetryPeriod <= 0`; dynamodb.go:161 `ticker := time.NewTicker(c.retry)` is the renew cadence; client-go comparator leaderelection.go:80 `if lec.RenewDeadline <= time.Duration(JitterFactor*float64(lec.RetryPeriod))`.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Operator sets ha.dynamodb: {lease_duration: 15s, renew_deadline: 10s, retry_period: 20s} — config validates clean. Leader A acquires at t=0; its first renew fires at t=20s, but the item expired at t=15s and standby B (polling acquire every 20s too) takes over somewhere in [15s, 35s]. Until A's tick returns ConditionalCheckFailed, both replicas run schedulers: a multi-second dual-emit window on EVERY leadership term, recurring silently, plus permanent leadership flapping (A can never hold a full term).

## Suggested direction

Add ha.dynamodb.retry_period < renew_deadline (client-go parity, which transitively gives retry < lease) to config.Validate with a table-driven test alongside the existing lease/renew check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] config.Validate rejects retry_period >= renew_deadline with a clear error
- [ ] Existing default (15s/10s/2s) still validates
- [ ] dynamodb.go:43's 'validated upstream' comment matches what is actually validated

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED

body:
## Problem

On an unrecognised non-retryable 4xx from the OTLP gateway, classify() returns ReasonUnknown, isTerminalHalt() is true, and the runner degrades the loop and fires EmitError(loop, rejectReason(err)) where rejectReason(ReasonUnknown) = "unknown_4xx" (runner.go:401). The critical EmitFailing alert matches kind=~"retryable_exhausted|checkpoint_load|checkpoint_save|checkpoint_fenced|granularity_unexpected|bad_encoding" — every terminal kind EXCEPT unknown_4xx. The rule's own description ("Any occurrence of these means data is being lost or the loop is stalled") and the emit taxonomy ("HALT + degrade" is supposed to be loud/alertable) clearly intend to cover this case; the kind string was evidently missed when the unknown-4xx halt path was added.

## Evidence

- `deploy/grafana/self-obs/alertrule-emit-failing.yaml:32`
- `deploy/grafana/self-obs/alertrule-emit-failing.yaml:24`
- `internal/schedule/runner.go:199`
- `internal/schedule/runner.go:401`
- `internal/schedule/runner.go:383-386`
- `internal/emit/CLAUDE.md:14 (Unknown → HALT + degrade + back off)`
- `deploy/grafana/README.md:85`

**Evidence**

```
runner.go:401 `return "unknown_4xx"` (ReasonUnknown) + runner.go:199-201 fires EmitError with that kind and degrades; alert expr: kind=~"retryable_exhausted|checkpoint_load|checkpoint_save|checkpoint_fenced|granularity_unexpected|bad_encoding" — no unknown_4xx.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

The Grafana Cloud emit token is rotated wrong (gateway starts returning 401/403 on POST /v1/metrics) or the gateway ships a novel err-mimir request-level 400. Every loop halts+degrades with emit_errors_total{kind="unknown_4xx"} — all product data flow stops — but the severity:critical EmitFailing alert never fires. Detection falls back to the severity:warning self-relative PollerStale alert (needs age > 2× the 6h p90 baseline AND > 300s), so the on-call gets a slower, weaker, un-attributed page for a total-outage condition.

## Suggested direction

Add unknown_4xx to the kind regexp in alertrule-emit-failing.yaml (and to the enumerations in its description and deploy/grafana/README.md's alert table). One-line artifact change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] alertrule-emit-failing.yaml expr matches kind="unknown_4xx"
- [ ] The rule description and deploy/grafana/README.md alert table enumerate unknown_4xx
- [ ] A grep/test (or the gen script, if the rules ever become generated) cross-checks the alert regexp against the rejectReason() kind strings in runner.go so a future kind can't silently miss alert coverage

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — Citation emit/CLAUDE.md:14 is slightly off — the "Unknown -> HALT + degrade + back off" line is at internal/emit/CLAUDE.md:16. One additional under-cited artifact: docs/alerts.md:98 also enumerates the fatal kinds (retryable_exhausted, checkpoint_*, bad_encoding) and likewise omits unknown_4xx, so the acceptance criteria should include docs/alerts.md alongside the rule description and README table. Also worth noting the inconsistency this surfaces: the self-obs dashboard's fatal-error panel and error-by-kind panel use kind!='collect' (an exclude-list), so they DO surface unknown_4xx — only the critical alert (an include-list) misses it, which is corroborating evidence the kind string was missed when the unknown-4xx halt path was added.

body:
## Problem

README.md:161-162: 'If your emit retry budget could exceed 120 s ... tune down `emit.retry_max` in your config to fit within the window.' No such field exists anywhere in internal/config (grep for retry_max finds only ha.dynamodb.retry_period); the emit retry budget is a hardcoded constant in the emitter. config.Load/LoadBytes uses `dec.KnownFields(true)` (config.go:373), so an unknown `emit.retry_max` key is a fatal load error.

## Evidence

- `deploy/ecs/terraform/README.md:161-162`
- `internal/config/config.go:373`
- `internal/emit/otlp/otlp.go:182`

**Evidence**

```
grep -rn "retry_max" internal/config → only `RetryPeriod yaml:"retry_period"` (ha.dynamodb); config.go:373 `dec.KnownFields(true) // unknown YAML key ⇒ error`.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator on EC2 launch type with a long drain window follows the README, adds `emit: { retry_max: ... }` to config_yaml, and every task crash-loops at startup with `load config: ... field retry_max not found` — a doc-induced outage of the deployment, with the operator believing they made a supported tuning change.

## Suggested direction

Fix the README to reference what actually exists (the fixed ~90s retry budget constant, or stopTimeout tuning), or add a real emit retry knob if per-deployment tuning is genuinely wanted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README no longer references emit.retry_max (or the knob exists in the schema and is generated into the example configs)
- [ ] Every config key named in deploy docs round-trips through config.LoadBytes

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — The README sentence begins on line 160 with the `emit.retry_max` token on line 161, so a slightly wider anchor (README.md:160-161) is more precise, but the cited 161-162 range captures it. Worth noting in the fix: the default retry budget (MaxElapsed = 5 min) already exceeds the 120 s stopTimeout by default and is not config-tunable at all — so the README both misstates the premise and names a nonexistent knob; the real levers are the hardcoded DefaultRetryPolicy constant or the module's stopTimeout.

body:
## Problem

The PORTKEY_API_KEY and LANGSMITH_API_KEY data entries (externalsecret.yaml:81-88) and the self-obs GC_SELF_* entries (:44-55) are rendered UNCONDITIONALLY, with `key: {{ .Values.externalSecrets.portkeySecret }}` etc. — empty values render `key: ""` (verified: `helm template --set externalSecrets.enabled=true` emits five empty `key:` lines with defaults). ESO cannot fetch a secret with an empty key, so the whole ExternalSecret sync fails and the target `genai-otel-bridge-secrets` Secret is never created. There is also no `required`/`fail` guard for aws.region or serviceAccount.esoName despite values.yaml declaring both 'Required when externalSecrets.enabled is true' — secretstore.yaml:13 instead silently defaults the region to "us-west-2", so a wrong-region store fails at sync time, not render time.

## Evidence

- `deploy/helm/templates/externalsecret.yaml:81-88`
- `deploy/helm/templates/externalsecret.yaml:44-55`
- `deploy/helm/templates/secretstore.yaml:13`
- `deploy/helm/values.yaml:461-462`
- `deploy/helm/values.yaml:469-470`

**Evidence**

```
helm template x deploy/helm --set externalSecrets.enabled=true → lines 582/586/590/599/603 of the render are `key: ` (empty). externalsecret.yaml:81-88 has no `{{- if .Values.externalSecrets.portkeySecret }}` gate, unlike the grafanaProductTokenSecret block at :21-39.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator deploys with ESO enabled for a Portkey-only environment (langsmithSecret left ""), the chart renders `LANGSMITH_API_KEY / remoteRef.key: ""`, ESO reports SecretSyncedError, genai-otel-bridge-secrets never appears, and all pods sit in CreateContainerConfigError (envFrom secretRef missing) — no telemetry flows even though every value the deployment actually needs was set. Similarly, forgetting aws.region silently targets us-west-2 instead of failing the render.

## Suggested direction

Gate each vendor data entry on its value being set (mirroring the grafanaProductTokenSecret pattern), and add `required`/`fail` checks for grafanaConfigSecret, grafanaSelfTokenSecret, aws.region and serviceAccount.esoName when externalSecrets.enabled — remove the silent us-west-2 default.

## Acceptance criteria

## Problem

On Kubernetes the mechanism works because kubelet expands `$(MEM_LIMIT)` inside the container args (`-container-mem-bytes=$(MEM_LIMIT)`, deployment.yaml:106). The ECS task definition sets a `MEM_LIMIT` environment variable (main.tf:305-308) but defines NO command/args — the image ENTRYPOINT is just `["/genai-otel-bridge"]` — and nothing in the binary reads MEM_LIMIT from the environment (grep: only the flag at main.go:56 feeds selfobs.SetMemoryLimit at :101, default 0 ⇒ no-op). The Go runtime itself only honours an env var literally named GOMEMLIMIT. So the main.tf comments ('Feeds GOMEMLIMIT = 80% of the limit (mirrors the Helm downward-API mechanism)') describe a mechanism that does not exist on ECS; the 80% figure is also wrong versus the code's 0.9 fraction.

## Evidence

- `deploy/ecs/terraform/main.tf:226-228`
- `deploy/ecs/terraform/main.tf:296`
- `deploy/ecs/terraform/main.tf:305-308`
- `cmd/genai-otel-bridge/main.go:56`
- `cmd/genai-otel-bridge/main.go:101`
- `deploy/helm/templates/deployment.yaml:106`
- `internal/selfobs/provider.go:102-107`
- `Dockerfile:33`

**Evidence**

```
main.tf:306-307: `name = "MEM_LIMIT" / value = tostring(local.mem_limit_bytes)` with no command/args in the container definition; main.go:56: `memLimit := flag.Int64("container-mem-bytes", 0, ...)`; grep of cmd/ + internal/ shows no os.Getenv("MEM_LIMIT").
```

## Failure scenario / impact

A Fargate task at the default 512 MiB runs with no GC memory ceiling. During emit backpressure (queue.max_batches=256 × ~1 MiB batches) or a large logs_export window, heap growth gets no GC backpressure and the leader task is OOM-killed instead of degrading gracefully — leader churn and an emit gap until the standby takes the DynamoDB lock, defeating the documented GOMEMLIMIT backstop (DESIGN §4.1) silently.

## Suggested direction

Either add `command = ["-config=/dev/null"...]`-style args — concretely `command = ["-container-mem-bytes", tostring(local.mem_limit_bytes)]` in the container definition (ECS command = docker CMD, appended to the ENTRYPOINT) — or rename the env var to GOMEMLIMIT (the Go runtime reads it natively; note it then bypasses the 0.9 headroom fraction, so prefer the args route). Fix the 80%-vs-0.9 comment either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A task launched from this module runs with GOMEMLIMIT ≈ 0.9 × memory (observable via runtime/debug or a startup log line)
- [ ] main.tf comments match the actual fraction and mechanism
- [ ] Helm path behaviour unchanged
- [ ] A task launched from the module runs with a soft memory limit actually applied (verifiable via runtime/debug.SetMemoryLimit(-1) in a test hook or a startup log line)
- [ ] tf comments match the real fraction and mechanism
- [ ] A gate/test that fails if the ECS container definition stops carrying the memory-limit wiring

**Also covers (same root cause):**
- ECS module never sets GOMEMLIMIT: MEM_LIMIT env is dead because the binary only reads the -container-mem-bytes flag and no command override exists

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — Minor: the mechanism narrative is exactly right, but worth noting the comment discrepancy is two-fold — main.tf:226-228 AND main.tf:296 both say "80%", while the code uses 0.9 (90%). The fix should correct both comments.

## Problem

The effective guard denylist is contentDenylist(optedInRecordFields(cfg)) (app.go:86), and optedInRecordFields reads ONLY settings["extra_record_fields"] (app.go:258) — gray backstop keys (error, name, events, extra, serialized, manifest, s3_urls, inputs_preview, outputs_preview) are subtracted only for that one knob. A gray key named in extra_indexed_fields or metadata_record_fields passes source validation (only hardDenied/floor keys are rejected — runs_settings.go:127-131, logs_settings.go:193-201) and passes the composition-root floor check (app.go:76-80 rejects floor keys only), is auto-allow-listed as a label, but stays on the deny map — and in okLog/ok deny beats allow (guard.go:98-104 runs before the allow check), so the WHOLE record/sample is dropped. This directly contradicts the code's own promise that a promoted indexed key "can't then be silently dropped by the default-deny guard" (app.go:62-64, echoed in logs_strip.go:110 / runs_strip.go:104) and followup.md:123's claim that a customer "CAN opt them in without the guard silently eating the whole record".

## Evidence

- `internal/app/app.go:86`
- `internal/app/app.go:248-266`
- `internal/app/app.go:276-296`
- `internal/app/app.go:62-64`
- `internal/source/guard.go:96-110`
- `internal/source/langsmith/runs_settings.go:127-131`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_settings.go:193-201`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_strip.go:219-247`
- `followup.md:123`
- `internal/source/guard.go:96-104`
- `internal/source/guard.go:141-148`
- `internal/app/app.go:65-79`
- `internal/app/app.go:200-205`
- `internal/app/app.go:63`
- `internal/source/langsmith/runs_settings.go:124-131`
- `internal/source/langsmith/runs_strip.go:104`

**Evidence**

```
app.go:258: `for f := range strings.SplitSeq(lp.Settings["extra_record_fields"], ",")` — the ONLY subtraction source; guard.go:98-104: `for _, m := range []map[string]string{lr.IndexedAttributes, lr.RecordAttributes} { for k := range m { if g.deny[k] { return false } } }` (deny beats allow). Verified: extra_indexed_fields="name" → "records produced by loop: 8; /v1/logs payloads emitted: 0"; metadata_record_fields="error" → "records produced by loop: 3; /v1/logs payloads emitted: 0".
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Empirically verified in a throwaway worktree against HEAD: (1) langsmith runs with settings.extra_indexed_fields="name" — Build succeeds, loop produced 8 records, 0 payloads reached the OTLP gateway (every LangSmith run has a name field, so the loop emits NOTHING forever, with only the guard_dropped counter as evidence); (2) portkey logs_export with settings.metadata_record_fields="error" — Build succeeds, 3 records produced, 0 payloads emitted (every record whose metadata carries that sub-key is dropped). Operator intent is silently neutralised — the exact failure mode the codebase fail-fasts floor keys to prevent.

## Suggested direction

Make the gray-tier subtraction consider all three opt-in knobs (extra_record_fields ∪ extra_indexed_fields ∪ metadata_record_fields), or reject a gray key in the two unsupported knobs fail-fast at Build (mirroring the floor check at app.go:76-80). Add regression tests mirroring TestLangsmithRunsExtraIndexedFieldFlows with a gray key.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A gray backstop key named in settings.extra_indexed_fields flows end-to-end (record emitted with the key as an indexed attr) OR Build returns a loud error naming the key
- [ ] A gray backstop key named in settings.metadata_record_fields lifts through as a record attr OR Build fails fast
- [ ] Regression tests cover both knobs with a gray key (e.g. name, error) and assert records are not silently guard-dropped
- [ ] app.go:62-64 / followup.md:123 claims match actual behaviour
- [ ] A config with langsmith runs extra_indexed_fields containing a gray-backstop key (e.g. 'error') is rejected at app.Build with an actionable error (or the key is deliberately released with a documented, tested decision)
- [ ] A regression test proves a promoted-and-allowed indexed key is never simultaneously on the guard's effective denylist
- [ ] The 'never silently dropped' comments at app.go:63 and runs_strip.go:104 are accurate after the fix

**Also covers (same root cause):**
- Promoting a gray-tier deny key via extra_indexed_fields (or governance.allow_label_keys) makes the guard drop every record carrying it — the exact 'never silently dropped' footgun the code claims is impossible

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — Minor imprecision, does not affect the finding: for the metadata_record_fields case the promoted key is NOT auto-allow-listed as a label (optedInIndexedFields reads only extra_indexed_fields, not metadata_record_fields). This is immaterial because RecordAttributes are not allow-list-policed by okLog anyway (guard.go:106-110 polices only IndexedAttributes); the drop is purely deny-driven in both cases. The extra_indexed_fields case IS auto-allow-listed as the finding states.

## Problem

config.LoadBytes applies defaults only for governance/profiling/dynamodb fields — never for LoopConfig.BucketSettle (the `helm:"default=10m"` tag is a chart-generation annotation only, as TestNewRejectsZeroWindow's comment itself notes: 'Load doesn't apply the chart default'). Validate has no settle>0 check for windowed loops (the M3 check at config.go:621 is trivially satisfied with settle=0), and newAnalyticsLoop accepts settle=0 (portkey.go:135) while it deliberately fail-fasts on window==0 (portkey.go:131). With settle=0, derive's settled cutoff = now (derive.go:115), so a bucket is emitted the instant it closes — before Portkey's measured ~185s late-arrival lag (DESIGN §15 OP5d) settles the value. Verified empirically: a config omitting bucket_settle loads and validates OK with settle=0. Meanwhile docs/portkey.md:63 tells operators there is a 'default 3 minutes' and DESIGN §15 says 'default 10m' — neither is implemented, so omitting the key looks safe.

## Evidence

- `internal/config/config.go:315`
- `internal/config/config.go:378`
- `internal/config/config.go:621`
- `internal/source/portkey/portkey.go:135`
- `internal/source/portkey/portkey.go:131`
- `internal/source/portkey/derive.go:115`
- `internal/source/portkey/derive.go:157`
- `docs/portkey.md:63`
- `docs/DESIGN.md:133`

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator hand-writes a source block (not from the Helm example, which sets 10m explicitly) and omits bucket_settle, trusting the documented default. Every 1-minute bucket is emitted at close with its incomplete first-observed value; late-arriving requests then revise the source bucket, but Mimir rejects any changed value at a settled (series,ts) — so requests/cost/tokens are systematically under-counted forever, with only the bucket_revised_after_settle counter hinting at it. This is a silent break of the emit-once-after-settle leg of the correctness contract.

## Suggested direction

Either default BucketSettle in LoadBytes (10m, matching DESIGN/Helm) or fail fast in newAnalyticsLoop when settle<=0 on a windowed loop (mirroring the window==0 rejection), plus a TestNewRejectsZeroSettle-style guard. Fix docs/portkey.md's 'default 3 minutes' to the real behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a windowed analytics loop with omitted/zero bucket_settle either gets the documented default or fails fast at build — never runs with settle=0
- [ ] a unit test covers the omitted-bucket_settle path
- [ ] docs/portkey.md states the actual default/requirement

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — Two mitigating facts worth noting for routing (do not negate the finding): (a) The Helm chart's generated values.yaml sets `bucket_settle: 10m` explicitly (via the tag + TestHelmGeneratedConfigUpToDate guard), and the ECS config example does too — so the primary/documented install paths are safe; the hazard is limited to fully hand-written configs that both omit the key AND trust the (wrong) prose docs. (b) detectionBand (portkey.go:179-185) floors the band at 1m, so even with settle=0 the `bucket_revised_after_settle` counter still fires for revisions landing within ~1m of close — partial observability survives, though the detection window is narrowed and revisions beyond 1m (up to the 185s lag) age out undetected. Severity stays medium: the correctness break is real and the docs actively assert a default that does not exist, but the recommended deployment paths are unaffected. Citations are all accurate as given.

## Problem

When the runs watermark is older than now-max_backfill, Collect clamps winMin to the floor with only slog.Warn — it never fires l.onGraphSkipped (unlike window_truncated at runs.go:230 and sessions_truncated at runs_discover.go:98). The scheduler's pre-emptive backfill_unstorable counter (scheduler.go:174) is gated on sp.Window > 0, but newRunsLoop REQUIRES LoopConfig.Window==0 (runs_settings.go:180) and the loop's real backfill knob is settings.max_backfill, not LoopConfig.MaxBackfill — so the scheduler count can never fire for this loop. The reactive ReasonTooOld path can't catch it either: the skipped span is never fetched, so nothing is ever emitted or rejected. followup.md:182 claims the pre-emptive backfill_unstorable_total is 'regression-tested for BOTH planes', but no langsmith runs test covers the floor path at all (only a settings-parse mention at runs_settings_test.go:44) and no counter exists on this path — doc-vs-code drift. Portkey logs_export has the identical warn-only pattern (logs_export.go:192-196) but at least has a backfill-clamp test.

## Evidence

- `internal/source/langsmith/runs.go:171-175`
- `internal/schedule/scheduler.go:174-176`
- `internal/source/langsmith/runs_settings.go:180 (Window must be 0)`
- `internal/app/app.go:144-145`
- `followup.md:182-184`

**Evidence**

```
runs.go:171-174: `if floor := now.Add(-l.maxBackfill); winMin.Before(floor) { slog.Warn("langsmith runs: watermark older than max_backfill — skipping the unstorable span", ...); winMin = floor }` — no hook call. scheduler.go:174: `if floor := now.Add(-sp.MaxBackfill); sp.Window > 0 && ... { s.m.SamplesSkipped(name, "backfill_unstorable", ...) }` with runs forced to Window==0.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Leader/vendor outage lasts 30h with max_backfill=24h. On recovery the runs loop silently (metric-wise) discards ~6h of run logs: one Warn log line, zero increment on any samples_skipped/graph_unavailable counter. window_lag returns to normal, dashboards show the loop healthy, and the operator concludes catch-up was complete — violating the 'every gap is alertable, never silent' hard rule (a log line is not alertable in this system's model).

## Suggested direction

Fire l.onGraphSkipped("runs", "backfill_skipped") (or a dedicated counter carrying the skipped-minutes magnitude like the scheduler's SamplesSkipped) inside the floor branch in runs.go, add a Collect test asserting it, and mirror the fix in portkey logs_export. Update followup.md's 'both planes' claim to match reality.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The runs.go max_backfill floor branch increments an alertable self-metric (not only slog.Warn)
- [ ] A test constructs a watermark older than now-max_backfill and asserts the counter fires and winMin is clamped
- [ ] followup.md/CLAUDE.md wording about pre-emptive backfill counting matches the code for the logs plane

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED

## Problem

usage.go:207-208 states as a live-probed fact: 'sort_by=start_time is required — a bare offset 403s on the real Cloudflare-fronted instance', and both the sessions loop (langsmith.go:342-343) and the usage loop (usage.go:217-218) set sort_by=start_time&sort_by_desc=true on every GET /sessions. But runs auto-discovery's listSessionIDs (runs_discover.go:58-63) sends only limit/offset/filter — no sort_by. One of two things is true, and both are defects: (a) the claim is accurate, so filter-bounded runs discovery 403s against the production Cloudflare-fronted LangSmith instance — every Collect fails at resolveSessions, the runs loop emits nothing while window_lag grows forever; or (b) the claim is false/overbroad, in which case a load-bearing in-repo probe fact is wrong and will mislead the next maintainer (and the 'mirrors the sessions loop's fetchPage query shape' comment is only half-honoured). Tests can't distinguish — all httptest fakes accept any query shape.

## Evidence

- `internal/source/langsmith/runs_discover.go:53-64`
- `internal/source/langsmith/usage.go:207-208`
- `internal/source/langsmith/langsmith.go:342-343`
- `internal/source/langsmith/usage.go:217-218`

**Evidence**

```
usage.go:207-208: '// Mirrors the sessions loop's fetchPage query shape (sort_by=start_time is required — a bare offset 403s'. runs_discover.go:58-61: `q.Set("limit", ...); q.Set("offset", ...); if l.sessionFilter != "" { q.Set("filter", ...) }` — no sort_by.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

A customer configures runs with session_filter (auto-discovery) instead of static session_ids against the WAF/Cloudflare-fronted instance the comment describes: listSessionIDs gets 403 on the first call, resolveSessions errors, Collect errors every tick, the runs loop delivers zero logs indefinitely (loud but totally non-functional), and the 403 also fires OnAuthError, misdiagnosing it as a credential failure.

## Suggested direction

Live-probe GET /sessions without sort_by on the real instance once. If required, add sort_by=start_time&sort_by_desc=true to listSessionIDs (also gives a defined pagination order); if not required, correct the usage.go comment so the probe record is accurate. Either way make the three /sessions call sites share one query-builder so they cannot drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] listSessionIDs' query shape is either proven-working against the real instance or made identical to the sibling loops'
- [ ] The usage.go probe comment matches observed server behaviour
- [ ] A single helper (or a test) keeps the three GET /sessions query shapes from diverging again

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — The failure scenario's claim that "the 403 also fires OnAuthError, misdiagnosing it as a credential failure" is WRONG for the discovery path. listSessionIDs returns a plain error on non-200 (runs_discover.go:74-78) without calling onAuthError; resolveSessions propagates it and Collect returns at runs.go:189, which is BEFORE the auth-error hook. onAuthError only fires on the runs/query response status (runs.go:202-203). So a discovery 403 surfaces as a loud retryable Collect error (window_lag grows) but does NOT emit the credential-failure (auth_errors_total) signal. Also note: the discovery query is materially lighter than the sibling loops' (no include_stats, no stats_start_time), so it is not certain the observed stats-query 403 applies to it — this is the residual uncertainty that a single live probe (per the finding's own suggested_direction) would resolve. The fix (share one query-builder across the three /sessions call sites, or add a test asserting identical shape) is valid regardless.

## Problem

The documented 'Example sessions config' sets `window: 1h` under loops.sessions. The sessions loop is a snapshot loop that must leave LoopConfig.Window unset (0) — the whole aggregate-now design. With window non-zero, config.Validate treats the loop as time-bucketed: 1h > maxWindow 55m → hard error 'window 1h > 55m (would flip bucket granularity, H5)'. So copy-pasting the official doc example makes the binary refuse to start. Additionally the example uses `session_filter: "my-app"`, but the filter is a LangSmith filter EXPRESSION — every in-repo example uses `eq(name, "my-project")` (settings.go:191); a bare project name passed verbatim as `filter` will 4xx or match nothing.

## Evidence

- `docs/langsmith.md:69-77`
- `internal/config/config.go:613-624`
- `internal/config/config.go:29 (maxWindow = 55m)`
- `internal/source/langsmith/settings.go:191 (correct filter grammar)`
- `docs/langsmith.md:72`
- `internal/config/config.go:29`
- `internal/config/config.go:616`
- `internal/config/config.go:611`
- `internal/source/langsmith/langsmith.go:98`

**Evidence**

```
docs/langsmith.md:72: `window: 1h` under `sessions:`. config.go:616-617: `if time.Duration(lp.Window) > maxWindow { errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("%s/%s: window %s > %s (would flip bucket granularity, H5)", ...)) }` with maxWindow=55m.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator onboards LangSmith following docs/langsmith.md verbatim: startup fails with 'window 1h > 55m'. If they 'fix' it by lowering to 50m instead of deleting the key, the snapshot loop silently ignores it while the scheduler flips into windowed semantics (see the companion Window-guard finding). If they keep `session_filter: "my-app"`, discovery/session scoping breaks against the real API grammar.

## Suggested direction

Remove the `window:` key from the sessions example (snapshot loops take stats_window inside settings) and change the filter examples to the `eq(name, "...")` grammar to match ExampleSource(). Consider a doc test that loads every fenced YAML example in docs/ through config.LoadBytes+Validate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] docs/langsmith.md sessions example passes config.Load + Validate verbatim
- [ ] session_filter examples in docs/langsmith.md use the same grammar as langsmith.ExampleSource()
- [ ] Optionally: a test parses doc YAML examples so they can't go invalid again
- [ ] the docs/langsmith.md sessions example passes config.LoadBytes + Validate verbatim
- [ ] the example uses settings.stats_window, not loop-level window
- [ ] (optional) a CI test loads all docs config examples through the real validator

**Also covers (same root cause):**
- docs/langsmith.md sessions example config is rejected by config validation (window: 1h trips the H5 55m cap on a loop that doesn't even use `window`)

Note the runs example's window: 1h (line 129) is NOT affected: it sits inside the settings: block (a langsmith runs setting string), not LoopConfig.Window, so it does not hit the maxWindow check — only the sessions-level window: 1h at line 72 fails.
