body:
## Problem

In the too-many-pages error path, createExport has already succeeded (a draft job exists server-side) before the page check errors and returns without persisting any cursor. Next tick re-enters stepIdle with the identical window and creates ANOTHER draft job, forever, until the operator shrinks `window`. Portkey has no delete API and cancel is invalid on a draft (400 AB01, logs_client.go:105-107), so the drafts accumulate; each create also consumes a shared-rate-limiter token every tick.

## Evidence

- `internal/source/portkey/logs_export.go:204-215`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_client.go:51-55`
- `internal/source/portkey/logs_client.go:105-108`

**Evidence**

```
logs_export.go:204 `jobID, total, err := l.createExport(...)` precedes :213-215 `if l.maxPagesPerWindow > 0 && pages > l.maxPagesPerWindow { return model.Batch{}, fmt.Errorf(...) }` — jobID is dropped, no cursor persisted, so the next tick repeats the create.
```

## Failure scenario / impact

Traffic grows so a 1h window needs >50 pages over a weekend -> at 60s cadence the bridge litters Portkey with ~1440 orphaned draft export jobs per day and burns one control-plane request per tick on a stall that cannot succeed, until an operator intervenes.

## Suggested direction

Persist a blocked marker in the cursor (window bounds + learned pages) after the first create so subsequent ticks re-raise the loud error from cursor state without re-creating the job; clear it when settings or the window change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the create endpoint is hit at most once for a window that exceeds max_pages_per_window while the error keeps being surfaced each tick
- [ ] The stall remains loud (error + window_lag) and recovers after `window` is shrunk

> **Verification:** CONFIRMED — Minor: the finding asserts cancel is "invalid on a draft (400 AB01)" citing logs_client.go:105-107; that comment actually only documents cancel as valid on queued/in_progress with a terminal job returning AB01 — it does not confirm the draft→AB01 behavior specifically. This is immaterial to the finding because the error path never attempts a cancel anyway; the orphan accumulates regardless of whether cancel would succeed on a draft. Also worth flagging for the fix author: at defaults (page_size=50000, max_pages_per_window=50) the trip threshold is ~2.5M logs per window, so real-world exposure is dominated by operators setting a smaller page_size or a very large window, not organic traffic growth.

body:
## Mission

Harden **`genai-otel-bridge`** for production and implement **every issue filed by the automated production-readiness bug bash** (2026-07-03), then ship the release. When the phases below are complete, [Project #3](https://github.com/users/rknightion/projects/3) is 100% done and both milestones are closed. Everything lands on `main` continuously; a release-please PR cuts the release — there is no interim-release ceremony.

**This issue is the kickoff + master tracker.** The orchestrating agent works from it directly — no scratch files. It launches the remainder: the phase plan below is the running order, the milestones are the phases, and the project board is the worklist. Progress lives here (see *Tracker protocol*) and on the individual issues, so any future session with **no memory of the bash** can resume from GitHub alone.

The bash swept the whole repo across 17 adversarial audit lanes + a completeness-critic pass; every candidate was independently refuted-or-confirmed by a second agent before filing. **112 open issues** (70 bugs → milestone #1, 43 improvements → milestone #2; #132 closed as a dup of #75). Each issue is a self-contained spec: `## Problem` / `## Evidence` (with `file:line`) / `## Failure scenario` / `## Suggested direction` (non-binding) / `## Acceptance criteria` / an adversarial-verification note.

- [Milestone #1 — bug fixes](https://github.com/rknightion/genai-otel-bridge/milestone/1) · [Milestone #2 — improvements](https://github.com/rknightion/genai-otel-bridge/milestone/2)
- Worklist query: `gh issue list --repo rknightion/genai-otel-bridge --milestone "Production-readiness — bug fixes" --state open`

## How to launch the remainder (orchestration model)

Modelled on the meraki v1 launch (rknightion/meraki-dashboard-exporter#618).

1. **The orchestrator is a scheduler, not an implementer.** It dispatches **one dedicated subagent per issue**, sequences the waves below, runs the mechanical gate, commits/pushes/closes on green evidence, and keeps this tracker current. It does not write code itself; a red `make gate` or a merge conflict spawns a scoped **fixer subagent**, it does not improvise.
2. **Model routing.** Correctness-contract seam issues (lanes A–E) and anything `security`-tagged → **Opus**. Everything else → Sonnet, with Haiku for pure doc-string/mechanical edits. Keep design + the final review on the main thread.
3. **One file = one owner (the only hard rule).** Lanes are cut along **disjoint file sets**. The seam files are **funnelled — a single owner per wave, never parallelised**: `internal/emit/otlp/*`, `internal/schedule/{runner,scheduler}.go`, `internal/checkpoint/*`, `internal/coordinate/*`, `internal/source/{guard,source,content}.go`, `internal/model/*`, and the composition root `internal/app/app.go`. Doc-drift (lane L) and deploy/CI (J/K) touch disjoint trees and parallelise freely.
4. **Freeze shared seams first.** Where several issues in a seam lane touch the same interface/helper (e.g. the reject taxonomy, the guard allow-list, `CheckMonotonic`), land the interface-shaping issue first and freeze the signature before fanning out the rest of that lane.
5. **Transient red mid-wave is fine; green is mandatory at each wave checkpoint and before every commit.** `make gate` green is evidence, not assertion.
6. **Subagents never commit or run `gh`.** Only the orchestrator commits (direct to `main`, `Closes #NN`, push immediately) and updates this tracker. Each subagent returns a self-contained final-message brief.

## Binding operating rules (from `CLAUDE.md` + the correctness contract)

1. **Read every issue IN FULL — body AND comments — first.** `Suggested direction` is non-binding; **re-verify the premise against current code** before implementing — line numbers cited on 2026-07-03 will have drifted, and a few issues may already be fixed (close stale ones with a note + a guard test rather than forcing a change).
2. **Strict TDD.** Reproduce the failure scenario as a failing test → watch it fail for the right reason → minimal fix → green → refactor. Many acceptance criteria already name the regression test.
3. **`make gate` green before EVERY commit** (vet + test + lint + forbidden-words + spdx-check + build); run `go test -tags acceptance ./internal/app/` when touching HA/schedule/emit/checkpoint seams.
4. **Direct to `main`.** Stage explicit paths (`git add <path>`), never `-A`/`.` (agents share the tree). `Closes #NN` in the completing commit; push immediately (bypass-on-push is expected).
5. **FROZEN-seam discipline.** No change to `model.*` types or `source.Source`/`source.Loop` without a matching `ARCHITECTURE.md` decision-ledger entry.
6. **Content minimisation is a release gate.** Never weaken the strips, the guard default-deny, or the two content-leak conformance gates. Treat any content-egress risk (#95 #96 #99 #103 #62 #111 #130 #139) as P0 regardless of its filed priority.
7. **Adversarially self-review each fix** before committing — attack it for the failure scenario in the issue and its inverse.

## Decisions already made — do NOT re-litigate

- **The correctness contract holds as designed:** conditional gap-free = deterministic byte-identical OTLP encoding + emit-once-after-settle + single-active-replica + monotonic lease-epoch-fenced checkpoint writes. Fixes must *strengthen*, never trade away, any leg.
- **Content-free is the enforced default** — do not build a content-emitting mode (`followup.md` §1).
- **Config-decoupling** — no vendor/customer/domain knowledge in core code or defaults.
- **OTLP is the sole emit wire format**; the `Emitter` interface is a test/queue seam only.

body:
## Symptom

Every push to \`main\` since \`1c940e0\` produces a \`release-please\` run with conclusion **startup_failure** (no jobs run, no logs). Last good run was on \`44c8c9e\`. This means the release PR is not being maintained.

## Root cause

\`release-please.yml\` calls \`publish.yml\` as a reusable workflow (\`uses: ./.github/workflows/publish.yml\`) from its \`publish\` job. In \`1c940e0\`, \`publish.yml\` gained a new \`wait-for-ci\` job that requests \`permissions: checks: read\` (it polls the \`ci-success\` check before an edge publish).

GitHub validates a called workflow's job permissions against the **caller job's** granted \`permissions\` block **at startup**, for *all* jobs, regardless of any \`if:\`. The \`publish\` caller job in \`release-please.yml\` grants \`contents/packages/id-token/attestations/security-events\` but **not** \`checks\` — so the reusable requests a scope the caller never granted, and the whole \`release-please\` run dies with \`startup_failure\`.

\`publish.yml\` running standalone (its own \`on: push\` trigger) is unaffected — there the workflow-level token is used, so \`wait-for-ci-success\` runs fine (and correctly fails the edge-publish gate when \`ci-success\` is red).

## Fix

- [x] Add \`checks: read\` to the \`publish\` job's \`permissions\` in \`release-please.yml\`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Next push to \`main\` produces a \`release-please\` run that starts and completes (not \`startup_failure\`), and maintains the release PR.

comments.body: Fixed in ef6c318 — added `checks: read` to the `publish` job's permissions in release-please.yml. Verified: the release-please run for e9bd784 now starts (`in_progress`) instead of `startup_failure`.

title: ci: release-please workflow fails at startup (startup_failure) since publish.yml gained wait-for-ci

body:
## Symptom

\`e2e / TestInvariant3_ZombieFrozenStandbyTakesOver\` fails on \`main\` (and therefore every Renovate PR branched from it), blocking \`ci-success\`:

\`\`\`
failover_test.go:134: resumed zombie's stale-epoch forward write was not observably fenced:
  no 'checkpoint forward-write fenced' evidence in pod ... logs
\`\`\`

The \`#138\` fence-evidence assertion was added in \`9dea560\` (bundled into the same push as \`4872de5\`, which was the CI tip) and has **never had a green CI run** — it was born red.

## Root cause

The assertion requires the resumed zombie to emit a \`checkpoint forward-write fenced\` warn. The production design correctly makes that warn unreachable in this scenario:

1. \`schedule.LoopRunner.commit()\` re-checks leadership (\`if ctx.Err() != nil { return }\`, tagged \`[ext-review-2]\`) **immediately before** \`cp.Save\`. \`commit\` is called with \`leaderCtx\`, which \`coordinate\` cancels on leadership loss. Once the resumed zombie's coordinate loop observes the lost lease and cancels \`leaderCtx\`, \`commit\` returns before \`Save\` — no \`ErrStaleWrite\`, no fence warn.
2. Even in the narrow window where \`Save\` does run, after the ~45s+ takeover the new leader's durable watermark is already **ahead** of the zombie's stale in-flight target, so the write lands in the *benign already-advanced* branch (\`durable >= attempted\`) — silent by contract (\`runner.go\` only warns when \`stored.Time.Before(w.Time)\`).

Both outcomes are correct, safe behaviour. The monotonic-frontier / no-rewind / new-leader-advances invariants the same test asserts **do** hold.

## Fix (decision: relax to best-effort)

- [x] Keep the SIGCONT resume step and the hard safety invariants (monotonic frontier, no rewind, new leader advancing).
- [x] Downgrade the fence-warn check to best-effort: \`t.Logf\` whether or not it appears; do not \`t.Fatalf\` on its absence.
- [x] Document why positive fence evidence is not reproducible here (leaderCtx gate + benign already-advanced).

## Acceptance

- [ ] \`e2e\` job green on the next push to \`main\`.

comments.body: Fixed in e9bd784 — relaxed the #138 fence-evidence check to best-effort (t.Logf, no t.Fatalf), keeping the monotonic/no-rewind/new-leader-advances invariants and the SIGCONT resume step as hard assertions. Rationale: the fence warn is unreachable here because commit() bails on the cancelled leaderCtx before Save ([ext-review-2]), and a long-frozen zombie's stale write is the benign already-advanced (silent) case. Watching the e2e job on this push.

body:
## Summary

`service.version` is set on the **OTLP metrics resource** (the MeterProvider's `Resource`), so it is promoted to a `service_version` **label on every emitted metric series**. Per the OpenTelemetry → Prometheus compatibility spec this is a deviation: version belongs on an **info metric** (`target_info` from the resource, or a `*_build_info` gauge), never as a label on ordinary series.

## The standard

Only `service.name` (+ `service.namespace`) → `job` and `service.instance.id` → `instance` are meant to become labels. **Every other resource attribute — including `service.version` — goes to a `target_info` metric** (OpenMetrics 1.0 convention). Promoting a resource attribute to per-series labels is a documented, non-default opt-in.

Consequence of putting version on every series: **each new build mints a whole new series set.** After a redeploy, the old-version and new-version series coexist for the query-lookback window, so any `sum`-style panel adds both → a transient multiplier; and active-series cardinality grows with the number of versions ever seen. This was found loudly on `graph2otel` (which runs a per-commit `:main` image) — see rknightion/graph2otel#104 for the full spec analysis. Repos on stable release tags hit the cardinality growth but rarely see the doubling.

## Change

- Keep `service.version` on the OTel **resource** (semconv-correct → flows to `target_info`).
- Stop it becoming a per-series label: rely on the existing `*_build_info{version=...}` gauge (and/or `target_info`) for version, joined via `group_left` where a panel needs it.
- Audit dashboards/alerts for any query that aggregates over or filters on `service_version` and repoint them at the info metric.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `service_version` no longer appears as a label on ordinary metric series (only on `target_info` / `*_build_info`)
- [ ] Version stays queryable via the build-info gauge (+ a documented `group_left` example)
- [ ] Dashboards/alerts updated if any referenced `service_version`
- [ ] Note the OTLP→Prometheus resource-attribute convention in the telemetry setup docs

Cross-repo consistency pass with rknightion/graph2otel#104 (detailed spec citations there). Sibling issues: tailscale2otel#187, opnsense-exporter#270.
title: Don't promote service.version to a per-series metric label (OTLP→Prometheus: version belongs on target_info/build_info)
